RagShortTexts: The death of Möngke Khan in 1259 halted Hulagu's Syrian advance, triggering Mongol civil war.

Variants.Content: In August 1259, Great Khan Möngke died during the siege of Diaoyu Fortress in Sichuan. The succession crisis shattered unified Mongol expansion: Hulagu withdrew the bulk of his western army from Syria to Azerbaijan, leaving Kitbugha with a depleted force, while Kublai and Ariq Böke plunged into civil war.

Möngke's demise was viewed across Cairo and Acre as a divine reprieve. The impending Mongol juggernaut stalled on the threshold of Egypt, providing Sultan Qutuz the narrow window needed to strike at Ain Jalut.

When messengers rode in with mourning scarves, the tumens turned eastward. Thousands of Mongol lancers abandoned Syrian campfires overnight, leaving only local garrisons to face the gathering Mamluk storm.
